text:
maria: Quick sync — did a pass this morning on onboarding XLM-13B-v2 (fp16, int8, int4) across our eval suites. TL;DR: big cost wins for int4 but we see measurable quality regressions on summarization and multi-hop QA. see details below.

aj: Thanks — can you paste the key numbers?

maria: Sure. Baselines are fp16-13B. Workloads: chat (interactive prompts), summarization (long-doc), rerank. Samples: 12k eval prompts from prod-shaped distributions.

maria: Perf/cost (per 1M tokens served, estimated infra cost):
- fp16: $420
- int8: $210 (~2x cost reduction)
- int4: $115 (~3.6x cost reduction)

maria: Latency (p50 / p95 / p99 for typical 8-token streaming step) on g5x: 
- fp16: 22ms / 48ms / 120ms
- int8: 26ms / 62ms / 150ms
- int4: 30ms / 80ms / 240ms

olga: p99 jump for int4 looks worrying for interactive SLAs. Do we know why p99 jumps that much?

maria: Two drivers: (1) kernel-side dequantization overhead on long contexts, (2) KV cache eviction thrash at high concurrency. We saw p99 correlate with sequence length > 1k and concurrent streams > 120.

sam: What about quality deltas? numbers, please.

maria: Quality (delta vs fp16 baseline):
- Summarization (ROUGE-L): int8 -0.6 pts, int4 -1.9 pts
- Multi-hop QA (exact match): int8 -0.9%, int4 -2.6%
- Rerank (pairwise AUC): int8 -0.4 pts, int4 -1.2 pts
- Human eval (semantic correctness, 800 samples): int8 ~neutral (slight noticeable drop in corner cases), int4 ~mildly worse (hallucination cases up).

aj: Those QA drops for int4 are non-trivial. What's the variance by prompt type?

maria: Int4 hurts long-context reasoning and arithmetic-like prompts the most. Short chit-chat or template responses are mostly fine.

devops-bot: Deploy report: 2026-03-18T09:22Z — canary run of 13B-int4 on dev cluster (20% traffic) completed. Error rate +0.12%, latency tail +15%.

olga: So what's your recommendation for rollout and routing?

maria: Proposed strategy:
1) Default route: int8 for interactive chat (all paid tiers), int4 allowed for low-SLA background workloads (batch summarization, embeddings precompute, rerank on lower-tier).
2) Canary & monitor: start with 10% traffic for int4 on non-critical orgs, enable quality regression alerts tied to our product testset (if delta >1.5 ROUGE or >1.5% EM then rollback).
3) Fallback policy: auto-fallback to int8 if confidence/heuristic fails or if p99 exceeds 180ms.
4) Optimization: enable KV cache pinning for long-doc flows to reduce p99, and limit concurrency per instance for int4 pools.

maria: Example routing policy (pseudo-config):
```
route:
  - if request.sla == "low" and workload == "batch": prefer model: xlm-13b-int4
  - if request.sla == "interactive": prefer model: xlm-13b-int8
  - fallback: xlm-13b-int8
metrics:
  quality_alert_thresholds:
    rouge_delta: 1.5
    em_pct: 1.5
  latency_p99_ms: 180
```

sam: Can we tighten int4 to certain prompt templates only? e.g., short completion and structured output where hallucination risk is low.

maria: Yes — we have prompt fingerprinting that classifies requests into "safe-for-quant" buckets. We can gate int4 by that classifier plus a confidence score. That reduces quality regressions ~40% in our sim.

aj: Unit economics note for GTN: show product teams the per-100k-user cost delta under three scenarios (fp16 only / mixed int8+int4 / int8-only). Can you produce those?

maria: Will do — I'll add a short slide with per-route cost curves and recommended default for startup customers (int8 for free-tier chat, int4 allowed for stored/async workloads).

olga: Any quick caveats for Dedicated or Private customers?

maria: Dedicated: easier to tune concurrency and KV pinning so int4 viable more broadly there. Private/on-prem: depends on kernel support; some GPU stacks have poorer int4 throughput — need validation per-customer.

sam: Sounds good. Please also add a one-line recommendation for GTN/solutions: "Use int4 for non-interactive batch and cost-sensitive rerank; prefer int8 for any user-facing interactive flows. Use prompt gating and automatic fallbacks to manage risk."

maria: adding that to the slide. Will post scorecard + CSV of raw evals in #eng-ml-results by EOD. :thumbsup: 

aj: Awesome — thanks. If you need infra help to set canaries, ping me and ops.

maria: will do.
